Duke Energy stock: BMO lifts target to $138 on rate clarity
sum: BMO Capital raised its price target for Duke Energy on Thursday, November 19, while maintaining an Outperform rating, according to Investing.com. The analyst moved the target to 138 US dollars from 128 US dollars after final orders in Duke Energy's North Carolina rate proceedings.

Duke Energy stock traded at 117.98 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 13:31 CET on Friday, November 20. The quote provides a current trading reference in euros, while BMO's target is stated in US dollars and reflects an analyst valuation rather than a market price.

BMO viewed the approved revenue requirement and ratemaking principles as a positive derisking event for Duke Energy. The North Carolina Utilities Commission approved the settlements in the company's rate proceedings, with an exception for the Large Load Tariff Settlement.

The analyst is monitoring tighter provisions in the large-load tariff. These include revised grandfathering terms, a stranded-generation charge and partial direct assignment of transmission upgrades. BMO also wants management commentary on how the rules could affect future large-load development in North Carolina.

The target change therefore combines regulatory visibility with continued scrutiny of the investment requirements attached to large data-center customers. For investors, the key issue is whether stronger customer protections can coexist with the capital spending needed to expand the grid.

The next major regulatory milestone is the implementation of the approved North Carolina rate changes, while the treatment of large-load customers remains an important variable for Duke Energy's grid investment outlook.

items.t: More for electricity NC | Duke Energy customers to see higher rates beginning in January 2027
sum: NORTH CAROLINA (WTVD) -- Duke Energy customers in North Carolina will see higher electric bills beginning in January after the North Carolina Utilities Commission approved rate increases for Duke Energy Carolinas and Duke Energy Progress.

For residential customers using 1,000 kilowatt-hours per month, Duke Energy Carolinas customers can expect bills to increase by $6.53 per month beginning in January, followed by an additional $4.66 per month in 2028.
Duke Energy Progress customers using the same amount can expect an increase of $9.62 per month in 2027 and another $5.89 per month the following year.

"People need to pay for food and shelter. Housing is going up, everything is going up. And it's very hard for people, working people, to make ends meet," said Donna Ford, a Henderson resident and member of Kerr Regional Citizen Voices.

"People's bills are going up. They're paying a greater percentage of their income for their electricity bills. The raise is going in effect in the middle of winter, when folks are going to need to turn the power on, turn the thermostat to keep it warm in the house," added Dan Crawford, Senior Director of Public Affairs with North Carolina League of Conservation Voters.
The Commission's order also establishes a new rate schedule for data center customers with loads above 50 megawatts and sets a 9.8% cap on Duke Energy's return on shareholder equity.

"We listened to our customers and worked closely with stakeholders to find a more cost-effective way forward. This outcome keeps affordability at the forefront while allowing us to make the investments needed to strengthen reliability and support North Carolina's continued growth. That balance is what we were working to achieve," Duke Energy North Carolina President Kendal Bowman said in a statement.

Donald Van der Vaart Resigns After Duke Energy Rate Decision
sum: North Carolina Utilities Commissioner Donald Van der Vaart will leave on January 1, days after a Duke Energy rate decision he opposed. He warned that residential customers could bear costs if data centers leave early. State Treasurer Brad Briner will appoint a replacement.
North Carolina Utilities Commissioner Donald Van der Vaart, a conservative regulator, is resigning effective January 1 after opposing a Duke Energy rate decision.
The decision allows Duke to raise residential bills by more than 9% over the next two years. Duke provides electricity to most of North Carolina.
Van der Vaart did not vote in the decision, though he filed a dissent. The commission did not give a reason for his nonparticipation in the vote.
The four other commissioners voted to approve the increase. Commissioners Floyd McKissick and John Gajda issued concurring opinions, while Van der Vaart was the sole dissenter.
Van der Vaart said he agreed with most of the decision. He argued, however, that it “does not reflect the risk this Order shifts from Duke to its customers.”

He raised concerns about rules included in the rate decision for data centers, facilities that use electricity to run computing equipment. He argued that ordinary customers could pay nearly half of a data center’s electric costs if its developer ended a contract early.

As winter heating season begins, Duke Energy shares simple steps to recognize natural gas leaks
sum: As outdoor temperatures fall and furnaces kick in, Duke Energy Ohio and Kentucky are reminding customers to know the signs of a natural gas leak and to take immediate action if they suspect one: If you smell natural gas, get out fast.

“Safety is our top priority at Duke Energy, and that means making sure our customers know how to recognize a potential natural gas leak,” said Amy Spiller, president of Duke Energy Ohio and Kentucky. “Understanding key warning signs, including mercaptan’s distinctive rotten egg odor, can help customers identify a leak and take appropriate safety precautions.”

Natural gas by itself has no smell. An odorant called mercaptan is injected into natural gas, giving it the distinctive smell of rotten eggs. The odor makes natural gas easy to detect and can alert the public of a natural gas leak to help avoid a potentially dangerous situation.

In addition to having a distinct smell, natural gas leaks can be visual, causing bubbling water, blowing dirt or dead plants. You may see sinkholes or exposed pipe. It’s also possible to hear a hissing sound near a leaking natural gas line or meter.
• Call Duke Energy at 800-634-4300 or call 911 from a neighbor’s house or somewhere away from the smell of natural gas.
• Do not return to the location of the leak until a Duke Energy technician or emergency responder informs you that the area is safe.

Installing a natural gas detector is an additional safety measure to keep residents aware of potential leaks. A natural gas detector, which can be purchased at major retailers and home improvement stores, will sound an alarm if levels of natural gas in the area indicate a leak.

sum: Duke Energy Florida filed plans on Tuesday, November 10, with the Florida Public Service Commission for four new solar energy sites. Duke Energy said the projects are intended to add 300 megawatts of clean generation and deliver an estimated 1 billion US dollars in customer savings over their operating lives.

The planned sites are Nova Renewable Energy Center, Bull Creek Renewable Energy Center, Hogeye Renewable Energy Center and Wewahootee Renewable Energy Center. They are located in Orange and Sumter counties, with construction scheduled to begin between January and May 2027.

The company expects the projects to enter service between February and June 2028. Duke Energy Florida said fuel-cost savings and production tax credits are expected to support the customer benefit cited in the announcement.

Duke Energy stock: SEC filing details January subsidiary merger
sum: Duke Energy's planned subsidiary reorganization has gained a more detailed legal outline. In a Form 8-K reporting an event from November 9, the utility said it expects to transfer its ownership interest in Duke Energy Carolinas to Progress Energy before combining Duke Energy Progress with Duke Energy Carolinas on January 1, 2027.

The filing from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission says Duke Energy Progress will merge into Duke Energy Carolinas, which will remain the surviving entity. Lenders consented to the combination through an amendment to the group's credit agreement.

The filing provides additional detail on the sequence of the internal steps. It describes a contribution of Duke Energy Carolinas to Progress Energy, followed immediately by the merger of Duke Energy Progress into Duke Energy Carolinas. The transaction concerns wholly owned subsidiaries and is not a merger of Duke Energy Corporation itself.

The planned completion remains January 1, 2027. For investors, the development is primarily an execution milestone tied to the utility's corporate and financing structure; the filing does not announce a purchase price or a new earnings target for the parent company.

sum: Duke Energy's third-quarter update, reported on Thursday, November 5, showed stronger earnings and a higher floor for its full-year outlook. The company posted adjusted earnings per share of 1.99 US dollars, up from 1.81 US dollars a year earlier, according to Ad Hoc News.

Infrastructure investment recovery and stronger electricity and natural-gas demand supported the quarter, while depreciation, interest expense, minority-interest effects and a higher effective tax rate were offsets.

Duke Energy prices $1.75B equity unit offering at $50 per unit
sum: Duke Energy completed a $1.75 billion public offering of 35 million equity units priced at $50 each. The units combine senior notes with stock purchase contracts, offering a 7.75% annual distribution. Proceeds will be used to redeem long-dated junior subordinated debentures and repay commercial paper.
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.

Duke Energy Corporation has priced a public offering of 35 million equity units at $50 per unit, raising an aggregate stated amount of $1.75 billion. The offering is expected to close on August 13, 2026. Each Corporate Unit consists of a contract to purchase Duke Energy common stock in the future, combined with two 1/40 undivided beneficial ownership interests in the company’s remarketable senior notes: one series due 2032 and another due 2036, both carrying a coupon rate of 4.85% and a principal amount of $1,000 per note.

The structure provides investors with total annual distributions at a rate of 7.75%, derived from interest payments on the senior notes and contract adjustment payments. Under the associated stock purchase contracts, holders are required to purchase a variable number of Duke Energy shares no later than August 1, 2029. The reference price for these contracts is set at $121.1827 per share, reflecting the closing price on August 10, 2026. The minimum settlement rate is 0.3301 shares, based on a threshold appreciation price of $151.4693 (a 25% premium over the reference price), while the maximum settlement rate is 0.4126 shares.

Duke Energy intends to list the Corporate Units on The New York Stock Exchange, with trading expected to commence within 30 days of issuance. The underwriters hold an option to purchase up to 5 million additional units, representing $250 million in aggregate stated amount, to cover over-allotments. If fully exercised, the total raised could reach approximately $1.965 billion after deducting underwriting discounts but before offering expenses.

The net proceeds, estimated at approximately $1,719 million, will be used to redeem $500 million of the company’s 3.25% Junior Subordinated Debentures due 2082. Additional funds will repay outstanding commercial paper and support general corporate purposes.

CHCI's first multifamily acquisition in North Carolina will be the third acquisition in 2026 under the Company's Institutional Venture Platform, following The Reed and Woodland Pointe

Comstock Holding Companies, Inc. (Nasdaq: CHCI) ("Comstock" or the "Company"), a leading real estate company specializing in the development, acquisition, operation, and management of mixed-use, transit-oriented properties and data center developments, today announced that it has entered into a purchase agreement to acquire The Ascher, a 672-unit Class A multifamily property located in Uptown Charlotte, North Carolina (the "Purchase Agreement"). Upon closing, which is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, The Ascher will join Comstock's growing portfolio of premier residential communities.

Opened in 2016, The Ascher includes two 24-story residential towers offering studio, 1, 2, and 3-bedroom floor plans, approximately 13,000 square feet of ground-floor retail, and a controlled-access parking garage with more than 900 spaces. The two buildings share a 6th-floor rooftop courtyard that includes a regulation tennis and pickleball court, a bocce court, a putting green, covered lounge seating with cafe tables, fire pits, grilling area, fenced-in dog parks, and an on-site pet spa. Each tower also includes its own private rooftop pool and sky terrace with panoramic city views, fitness center, resident clubhouse and lounge, and grilling area. In-unit amenities include floor-to-ceiling windows, private balconies, well-equipped kitchens, and washers/dryers.

sum: Duke Energy has delivered a 3 year share price gain that is hard to ignore, yet the real question for investors is whether today's US$120.67 price lines up with the dividend stream that underpins the stock. With income still a central reason many people own utilities, the focus now turns to what that payout really justifies.
- The stock is up 53.3% over the past 3 years, which puts real pressure on the dividend case to explain why the equity has become this valuable.

- Duke Energy's recent agreement on data center costs with Amazon, Google, Meta, and Microsoft may support future capital spending and could influence how much cash is available for dividends over time.
- If you'd rather focus on earnings, this one's for you. See why Duke Energy's 18.2x P/E tells a different valuation story.
The issue now is whether the current share price is adequately supported by the dividend stream that the Dividend Discount Model (DDM) attributes to Duke Energy.
If you are weighing Duke Energy's valuation against its dividend stream and data center exposure, it can help to compare that lens across 42 power grid technology and infrastructure stocks

The Dividend Discount Model (DDM) looks at what Duke Energy's future dividend stream could be worth in today's terms. For this utility, the model leans on a current dividend per share of about $4.61, a reported return on equity of 9.21%, and a payout ratio a little above 71%. That combination yields an implied dividend growth rate near 2.7%, which is a relatively modest pace and broadly in line with a mature, capital intensive electricity provider.

Duke Energy stock: BTIG cuts Duke Energy stock target to USD 135
sum: Duke Energy stock (ISIN US26441C2044) was hit by a BTIG target cut from USD 141.00 to USD 135.00 on October 20, 2026, according to TipRanks. At Lang & Schwarz, the stock was trading at EUR 108.18 on October 21, 2026 at 4:41 p.m. CEST.

BTIG analyst Alex Kania retained a Buy rating while lowering the target to USD 135.00 from USD 141.00. The note previewed Duke Energy's third-quarter results and cited interest rates as a headwind on utility valuations, while also pointing to longer-term demand from large electricity loads, according to TipRanks.
A second October 20 note was more cautious. BofA lowered its target from USD 138.00 to USD 127.00 and kept a Neutral rating ahead of the quarterly report, as Markets Insider reported.

Duke Energy generated USD 7.59 billion of revenue in the second quarter of 2026, an increase of 1.10 percent from the year-earlier period. MarketBeat also reported adjusted earnings per share of USD 1.43 for the quarter, above the consensus estimate of USD 1.30, with revenue up 1.10 percent year over year.

As of October 21, 2026, Duke Energy had a market capitalization of USD 94.84 billion, a P/E ratio of 18.26 and a dividend yield of 3.57 percent. Its 52-week range was USD 112.40 to USD 134.49. The range places the stock below its yearly high while keeping the price above the low.

Duke Energy will publish third-quarter 2026 results at 7:00 a.m. ET on November 5, 2026, followed by an analyst conference call at 10:00 a.m. ET. The date was announced by Duke Energy on October 6, 2026.

The November report will test whether the 1.10 percent second-quarter revenue increase and the USD 1.43 adjusted earnings per share result can support the longer-term growth case cited by BTIG. The contrast between BTIG's USD 135.00 target and BofA's USD 127.00 target gives investors a clear measure of the disagreement over valuation.
